from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

            "We need a way to measure instantaneous change."
        ])
        
        # Load Assets
        car = ImageMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/car.png")
        speedometer = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg")
        
        # Elements
        self.place_in_area(car, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        dynamic_dot = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        self.place_at_grid(dynamic_dot, "D3", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        discrepancy_group = VGroup(speedometer)
        self.place_in_area(discrepancy_group, "C4", "E5", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(car))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(dynamic_dot))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(discrepancy_group))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Derivative: Magnifying the Instant", [
            "We zoom in on the cheetah's position curve.", 
            "As we zoom, the curve looks straight.", 
            "This straight line represents instantaneous velocity."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        cheetah = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/cheetah.svg")
        
        # Setup Curve - Fixing according to Critic (Issue 24)
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.1 * x**3, x_range=[-3, 3], color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(curve, "B3", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        cheetah.scale(0.5).next_to(curve.get_start(), UP)
        self.play(Create(curve), FadeIn(cheetah))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Fixing point placement according to Critic (Issue 25)
        dot = Dot(color="#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(dot, "D4", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.add(dot)
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        # Zooming effect
        self.play(curve.animate.scale(2).move_to(dot), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fixing tangent placement according to Critic (Issue 26)
        tangent = Line(start=LEFT*1, end=RIGHT*1, color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(tangent, "C3", "E5", scale_factor=0.7)
        
        self.play(Create(tangent))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        # Cheetah moves along tangent
        cheetah.move_to(tangent.get_start())
        self.play(MoveAlongPath(cheetah, tangent), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Calculating areas of curves is inherently difficult.", "We approximate the area using tiny rectangles.", "Summing these rectangles gives the total area."]
        self.setup_layout("The Integral: Summing the Infinite", lecture_lines)
        
        # Setup Axes and Curve
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2, x_range=[0, 4], color=WHITE)
        
        # Applying layout fixes from VideoCritic
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'D1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.45)
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'D2', 'F6', scale_factor=0.45)
        
        # Load asset
        rect_svg = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rectangle.svg")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(axes), Create(curve))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Use rect_svg to represent the approximation
        rects = VGroup(*[rect_svg.copy().scale(0.2) for _ in range(6)])
        # Position them crudely for illustration
        for i, rect in enumerate(rects):
            rect.move_to(axes.c2p(0.5 + i * 0.5, 0.25 * (0.5+i*0.5)**2))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(FadeIn(rects.set_color("#FF00FF")))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        # Increase rect density
        rects_dense = VGroup(*[rect_svg.copy().scale(0.1) for _ in range(12)])
        for i, rect in enumerate(rects_dense):
            rect.move_to(axes.c2p(0.25 + i * 0.3, 0.25 * (0.25+i*0.3)**2))
            
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(rects, rects_dense.set_color("#00FF00")))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Fundamental Theorem: The Bridge", [
            "Differentiation and integration are inverse processes.",
            "One breaks down, the other adds up.",
            "They form the foundation of calculus."
        ])
        
        # Define objects
        derivative_symbol = MathTex(r"\\frac{d}{dx}f(x)", color="#FFFFFF")
        integral_symbol = MathTex(r"\\int f(x) dx", color="#FFFFFF")
        # Load asset
        bridge = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/bridge.svg", color="#FFFF00")
        
        math_group = VGroup(derivative_symbol, bridge, integral_symbol).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Using recommendation 31/32 for balanced layout
        self.place_in_area(math_group, 'C2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.85)
        self.play(FadeIn(derivative_symbol), FadeIn(integral_symbol))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(bridge))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        arrow1 = Arrow(start=derivative_symbol.get_bottom(), end=integral_symbol.get_bottom(), color="#FF0000")
        arrow2 = Arrow(start=integral_symbol.get_top(), end=derivative_symbol.get_top(), color="#FF0000")
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow1), GrowArrow(arrow2))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF0000"))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Calculus studies continuous change in our world.",
            "It predicts the behavior of dynamic systems.",
            "It is the core language of science."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion: The Language of Change", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create elements
        planet = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/planet.svg", color=WHITE)
        math_symbols = VGroup(
            MathTex(r"\int", color=WHITE),
            MathTex(r"\frac{d}{dx}", color=WHITE),
            planet
        )
        math_symbols.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(math_symbols, 'B3', 'C5', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        system = VGroup(
            Circle(radius=1.0, color=BLUE),
            Dot(color=TEAL),
            Line(ORIGIN, UP*1.2, color=BLUE)
        )
        self.place_at_grid(system, 'D4', scale_factor=0.8)
        system.set_opacity(0)
        
        microscope = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/microscope.svg", color=YELLOW)
        concept = VGroup(
            Text("Calculus = Language of Science", font_size=32, color=YELLOW),
            microscope
        )
        concept.arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(concept, 'D2', 'D5', scale_factor=0.7)
        concept.set_opacity(0)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(math_symbols))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(system))
        self.play(
            FadeOut(math_symbols),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF")
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(concept))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Essence of Calculus: From Discrete to Continuous
outline.target_audience: High school students or introductory university students

sections.title: The Hook: The Limits of Average
sections.content: Introduce the problem of measuring speed. Explain that average speed (total distance / total time) fails to describe the instantaneous state of motion. Establish the prerequisite: Understanding linear slope (rate of change).
sections.example: A cheetah chasing prey: 'Average speed' tells us how fast it ran over 10 seconds, but not how fast it was going at the exact moment it pounced.

sections.title: The Derivative: Magnifying the Instant
sections.content: Visualize the 'Zooming In' process. As the time interval shrinks toward zero, the secant line on a graph morphs into a tangent line. This is the birth of the derivative: measuring instantaneous change.
sections.example: An animation showing a curve of the cheetah's position; as we zoom in on a single point, the curve looks like a straight line, representing the instantaneous velocity.

sections.title: The Integral: Summing the Infinite
sections.content: Introduce the area problem. Explain that while it's easy to calculate the area of rectangles, curved shapes are difficult. We approximate using many thin rectangles; as their width approaches zero, the sum becomes the 'Integral'.
sections.example: Calculating the total distance traveled by a robot whose speed changes constantly by summing the tiny 'area' strips of speed × time under its velocity-time graph.

sections.title: The Fundamental Theorem: The Bridge
sections.content: Reveal the 'Secret Connection': Differentiation (breaking things down) and Integration (putting them together) are inverse processes, much like addition and subtraction.
sections.example: Visualizing the robot's journey: Integrating the velocity curve gives us the total distance traveled, while differentiating the distance curve gives us back the velocity.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Language of Change
sections.content: Summarize that calculus is the mathematical study of continuous change. It allows us to predict the future of dynamic systems, from planetary orbits to AI optimization.
sections.example: A final visual showing how calculus allows us to calculate not just where a rocket is, but exactly how much fuel it needs to land precisely on a moving platform.
